prompt.context: Our client is a highly diversified US multinational company interested in investing in a new Brazilian highway. It would be the company's first investment in Brazil. The highway is currently being built.
prompt.question: Should the client proceed with this investment?

clarifying_info.q: How long is the highway / where is it located?
clarifying_info.a: The highway stretches between two population centers, each with 750,000 inhabitants.

clarifying_info.q: What kind of vehicles does it allow?
clarifying_info.a: It takes only passenger cars, not trucks.

clarifying_info.q: How many inhabitants would use this highway?
clarifying_info.a: 1/3 of inhabitants in each city have cars.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected usage of the highway?
clarifying_info.a: The car-owning inhabitants make on average one roundtrip voyage between the two cities per year.

clarifying_info.q: How much is the company planning to invest?

exhibits.title: Case page (no standalone data exhibit)
exhibits.shows: The PDF page containing the case stem and Phase 1 background text; no separate data table or chart is present.
exhibits.data: Investment amount: $10M; highway connects two cities of 750,000 inhabitants each; 1/3 car ownership; one roundtrip per car-owner per year

framework: Understand the asset: highway characteristics, location, traffic potential
Estimate demand: population, car ownership, usage frequency → total trips
Identify revenue streams: tolls, rest stops, billboard advertising
Calculate annual profit from each revenue stream
Assess payback period: total investment / annual profit
Evaluate risks and strategic fit: political/country risk, portfolio synergies, entry into South America

questions.prompt: Estimate the number of one-way trips on the highway per year.
questions.guidance: 750,000 inhabitants per city × 1/3 car ownership = 250,000 car-owners per city. Both cities combined = 500,000 cars. Each makes one roundtrip per year = 500,000 roundtrips = 1,000,000 one-way trips.

math.setup: 2 cities × 750,000 inhabitants × (1/3) car ownership × 1 roundtrip/year × 2 one-ways/roundtrip

questions.prompt: Calculate annual profit from the three revenue streams: tolls, rest stops, and billboard advertising.
questions.guidance: Tolls: $1 per one-way trip × 1M trips minus $250K operating cost. Rest stops: $1.2M revenue minus $375K cost. Billboards: 100 billboards × $10K × 80% occupancy, no costs. Sum for total annual profit.

math.setup: Tolls profit = (toll revenue) - (tollbooth operating cost); Rest stop profit = revenue - maintenance; Billboard revenue = 100 × $10K × 80%

questions.prompt: How long will it take to recoup the $10M investment?
questions.guidance: Divide total investment by annual profit. Answer should be stated in years and months.

steps: 0.21 years × 12 months ≈ 2.5 months, round to ~3 months

brainstorming.prompt: What other risks and considerations would you take into account when assessing this opportunity?

categories.name: Operational / Execution Risk
ideas: Construction delays on the highway currently being built
Safety and security on the highway (crime)

categories.name: Demand Risk
ideas: Overestimation of car ownership or trip frequency
Competition from alternative routes or transport modes

categories.name: Strategic Fit
ideas: Synergies with existing portfolio of a diversified multinational
This being the company's only Brazilian operation — concentration risk vs. entry foothold

recommendation: Proceed with the investment. The payback period of approximately 4 years and 3 months is attractive, and the three revenue streams (tolls, rest stops, billboards) are diversified and appear reliable given the captive traffic between two sizeable population centers.
risks: Political instability and regulatory risk in Brazil
This is the client's first and only Brazilian operation, leaving it exposed without a broader local presence
Revenue assumptions (car ownership, trip frequency, billboard occupancy) may prove optimistic
Highway serves only passenger cars, limiting volume upside
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on Brazilian regulatory and political environment
Explore whether additional Brazilian investments could spread country-specific fixed costs and risk
Model downside scenarios (e.g., 60% billboard occupancy, lower trip frequency) to stress-test payback period
Identify whether the highway investment creates strategic optionality for further South American expansion
